**Setting up a strong organizing and outreach plan comes with many costs.**

Here’s a breakdown of the categories we’re focusing on going into the summer:
**Polling** – national polling struggles to tell the complete story, but targeted polling in key political geographies (like the Philly suburbs!) gives us a more nuanced, more granular understanding of the electoral climate.

_How are independent voters feeling about a Biden-Trump rematch? Are undecided voters leaning a particular way? How many might skip November’s election entirely?_ Polling will help us answer these questions – and we need this information to target our field efforts effectively.
**[Donate to fund polling costs>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/84948083/473155280/120714406?amount=25&refcode=05142024_md_mmfr_fr_1&refcode2=95484091-2c12-ef11-96f3-6045bdd9e096&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDQ1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NTQ4NDA5MS0yYzEyLWVmMTEtOTZmMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=DeocatBkBZzabFq8J32XPCbVwLqrlrCY9mBrz-tEscU=)**
* * *
**Printing materials** – we have volunteers, staff, and partner organizations/campaigns ready to help us reach voters – and that means we need to print palm cards, yard signs, buttons, and more to amplify our message. Folks who receive printed materials from a campaign are more likely both to get involved _and_ to vote. And we need to turn out voters for races up-and-down the ballot – which means we’ll be going through a lot of printed materials!
**[Donate to fund printing costs>>](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/84948086/473155281/120714406?amount=25&refcode=05142024_md_mmfr_fr_1&refcode2=95484091-2c12-ef11-96f3-6045bdd9e096&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDQ1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NTQ4NDA5MS0yYzEyLWVmMTEtOTZmMy02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=DeocatBkBZzabFq8J32XPCbVwLqrlrCY9mBrz-tEscU=)**

#
---
Team, No race is more important to our chances of holding the Democratic Senate majority than Montana. name: Josh Harder
subject: Michael Cohen’s testimony
body:
Reaction from MAGA world.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/84949493/473158766/-1463099547?refcode=-header-&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWMyZDAxM2MtMmUxMi1lZjExLTk2ZjMtNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=NxqBs8xK2Cg5suTYdjqt9Z2UmiB8jCI-SW4tqB4U5sQ=) | Peter, It’s been another crazy week in Donald Trump’s criminal trial. Yesterday, his former lawyer and self-proclaimed “fixer” Michael Cohen took the stand. He told the jury that Donald Trump directed him to pay Stormy Daniels in order to keep her silent before the 2016 election. What I find most revealing isn’t what Michael Cohen said however. It’s the reaction from MAGA world. Instead of defending Donald Trump with facts (you know, in the court of law), today a line of MAGA celebrities rushed to the courtroom to... hold a very weird press conference. Speaker Mike Johnson (fresh off his trip to my district) plus a long list of potential VP picks turned the courtroom into a campaign stop. Each of them - Doug Burgram, Vivek Ramaswamy, Bryon Donalds - all took to the microphone to attack the Judge, the witnesses, and the Department of Justice. None tried to defend Trump on his actions or virtues. I think that says something. They think Trump is going to win, and they have to prove their loyalty. And look, they might not be wrong. Vicente Gonzalez, a life-long Democrat, is a candidate for Texas’ 34th U.S. Congressional District.
From humble beginnings, Vicente was raised in a military family. Through hard work and pure ganas, Vicente aimed to make something of himself. His mother stressed to him over and over again that education was the key that will open doors of opportunities. A note from Kirsten: Friend, I can’t thank you enough for standing by my side in the critical fights ahead of us. As Democrats face our toughest Senate map in decades, I need your help more than ever. While Republicans only have to defend 10 seats in 2024, Democrats have to defend 23 — and if the GOP flips just two of them, it will deliver Senate control back to Mitch McConnell. Now, experts at FiveThirtyEight are saying that the GOP has a clear path to the majority. Fellow American - my name is Curtis Bashaw, and I am running for Senate in a major sleeper race, where we have the opportunity to make history and flip this seat for the first time since 1972.

**_In a moment I am going to ask you for a critical donation ahead of our mid-month fundraising deadline, but let me explain first why your support is so crucial._**

In high school, I started working as a bellhop and waiting tables at Congress Hall in Cape May. Since then, I’ve been working nonstop. I started a business 35 years ago and am a proud job creator, employing more than 1,000 hard-working people today.

As an entrepreneur, I have the responsibility of making a payroll every two weeks, and I know that people’s car payments, rent, and mortgages depend on me and our team effectively doing our job. It’s never been easy, _but it’s always been worth it._

| **_GET TO KNOW CURTIS_**

**Curtis Bashaw is a hotel entrepreneur, job creator, and preservationist. He’s running for United States Senate to provide greater freedom and opportunities for all New Jerseyans.**

A lifelong New Jersey resident, Curtis grew up in Camden County and spent his summers at the Jersey Shore working as a bellhop and waiting tables at Congress Hall in Cape May. He has spent his life in the real estate and hospitality industries, and is the Founder and Managing Partner of Cape Resorts, a hotel company focusing on the restoration and operation of classic American resort properties in New Jersey and New York.

Throughout his career, Curtis has worked to build communities and bring people together. He is widely recognized for leading the landmark restorations of Congress Hall and the Virginia Hotel in Cape May, and for launching creative programming to dramatically extend Cape May’s season, a catalyst for the economic rebirth of one of the Jersey Shore’s most beautiful communities.

Curtis is a successful businessman and job creator, employing more than 1,000 people in New Jersey and New York. Curtis’ company owns and operates eight hotels, ten cottages, six restaurants, four retail outlets and a working farm, all on the Jersey Shore and Long Island’s East End. Curtis lives in Cape May with his husband, Will.

| | | **Honor Their Sacrifice: Support Peace Officers Memorial Day**
---

Dear Peter,
Tomorrow, on Peace Officers Memorial Day, we stop to remember and honor the brave law enforcement officers who have made the ultimate sacrifice in service to our community. Their dedication to protecting and serving Washington's 8th district reflects the highest ideals of courage and commitment. Let us pause and remember their selflessness in serving and protecting our communities.
Our campaign is committed to ensuring that our law enforcement personnel have the support they need to safely and effectively perform their duties. We are focusing on promoting policies that enhance officer safety, foster community relations, and honor the memory of fallen heroes.
---
| | | |
---
|
In tribute to these valiant officers, we invite you to make a special contribution to our campaign.
Your donation of $25, $50, or $100 will empower Carmen to advocate for legislation that supports our police force and enhances public safety across our district.

With deepest respect,

Team Goers

| | I have more good news to share thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law: our region is receiving significant support for our seaports and airports! **First, the U.S. Department of Transportation's Federal Highway Administration has granted $16 million to the Northwest Seaport Alliance.** Grants like this one are essential in transitioning our operations to zero emissions, supporting not only our environment but also our truck drivers with the necessary charging infrastructure. This funding will:
* provide incentives for the purchase of 36-58 heavy-duty, zero-emission trucks;
* fund the operation of those trucks along with the charging or fueling infrastructure needed to support those vehicles in our region; and
* reduce truck air pollution near the Ports of Seattle and Tacoma, benefiting truck drivers, port workers, and families in our communities.

The Northwest Seaport Alliance has set ambitious goals to eliminate seaport-related emissions by 2050, and this funding is a crucial step toward building a cleaner future while keeping our economy moving. **Furthermore, the Friday Harbor Airport, Lopez Island Airport, and Anacortes Airports have secured $2.8 million in AIG funding to modernize airport infrastructure, improve runway safety, and create jobs.** Additionally, the FAA granted $1,000,001 to the Port of Friday Harbor to improve its fuel farm infrastructure. This investment is crucial for enhancing safety and accommodating more aircraft. These are just a few of the over 670 specific projects identified for funding statewide. clean_body: Building a cleaner future while keeping our economy moving. | | | | I have more good news to share thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law: our region is receiving significant support for our seaports and airports! First, the U.S. Department of Transportation's Federal Highway Administration has granted $16 million to the Northwest Seaport Alliance. Grants like this one are essential in transitioning our operations to zero emissions, supporting not only our environment but also our truck drivers with the necessary charging infrastructure. This funding will: provide incentives for the purchase of 36-58 heavy-duty, zero-emission trucks; fund the operation of those trucks along with the charging or fueling infrastructure needed to support those vehicles in our region; and reduce truck air pollution near the Ports of Seattle and Tacoma, benefiting truck drivers, port workers, and families in our communities. The Northwest Seaport Alliance has set ambitious goals to eliminate seaport-related emissions by 2050, and this funding is a crucial step toward building a cleaner future while keeping our economy moving. Furthermore, the Friday Harbor Airport, Lopez Island Airport, and Anacortes Airports have secured $2.8 million in AIG funding to modernize airport infrastructure, improve runway safety, and create jobs. Additionally, the FAA granted $1,000,001 to the Port of Friday Harbor to improve its fuel farm infrastructure. This investment is crucial for enhancing safety and accommodating more aircraft. These are just a few of the over 670 specific projects identified for funding statewide. I am committed to building a stronger, more resilient future for Northwest Washington, and I am proud to have played a role in securing $8.7 billion in Bipartisan Infrastructure Law funding for Washington state. | | **For Immediate Release:** May 14, 2024
**Contact:**[press@davemin.com](mailto:press@davemin.com)
**This Police Week The Choice is Clear - Police Endorsed Candidate Dave Min or Career Criminal Scott “Defund the Police” Baugh**
**IRVINE, CA** — In recognition of Police Week, California State Senator Dave Min celebrates the dedication and service of local law enforcement officers. A long-term ally of law enforcement, Dave started his career at the Securities and Exchange Committee as an Enforcement Attorney, collaborating with the FBI to prosecute financial fraud, and as a State Senator, he has staunchly supported police by authoring bills on retail theft, public transit safety, and domestic violence support, and securing $1 million for local police funding.

**"Police Week is a time to recognize the sacrifices made by our law enforcement officers who put their lives on the line every day to keep our communities safe,"** said Senator Min.**"I’m proud to be able to say I’ve spent my career fighting for law enforcement, whether it was prosecuting Wall Street criminals at the SEC or as a State Senator standing with police. My career and legislative record stand in stark contrast to my opponent Scott Baugh, a career criminal who tried to defund the police when he was Chair of the Orange County Republican Party and who supports a $17 billion cut to federal police funding. Unlike Scott Baugh, I’m proud to stand with police officers and I’m honored to have their support in this race.”**

Min is the clear choice of Law Enforcement in the CA-47 Congressional race. Min is proudly endorsed by:
* [Peace Officers Research Association of California (PORAC)](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=d6a9263dff&e=7017cc100e)
* [Los Angeles Police Protective League (LAPPL)](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=a1669b0bf2&e=7017cc100e)
* [Association of Los Angeles Deputy Sheriffs (ALADS)](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=56b13e75bf&e=7017cc100e)
* [The California Lodge of the Fraternal Order of Police](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=2de0b3c446&e=7017cc100e)

Min’s strong public safety record, and support from law enforcement stands in stark contrast to disgraced lobbyist Scott Baugh, whose criminal and anti-police actions extend to both his personal and professional life.

Scott Baugh’s Record of Opposing Law Enforcement
* As Chairman of the Orange County Republican Party, Baugh used his position to try to defund the police [by instituting a rule that any Republican candidate who supported the police unions would automatically be barred from the party’s endorsement](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=c4e99c45c6&e=7017cc100e).
* Today, while claiming to "back the blue," Baugh is backed by extremists on the Republican Study Committee whose budget proposal, aims to defund the Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) Program, revealing a disconnect between his rhetoric and the reality of his legislative priorities. Meanwhile, Baugh’s colleagues in the House GOP [have proposed a staggering $17 billion in cuts](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=a394ccc52a&e=7017cc100e) to federal law enforcement, courts, and prisons that support public safety.
* Baugh began his career as a corrupt State Assemblymember, engaging in campaign finance fraud, perjury, and obstruction of justice, [which led to his being indicted for 22 criminal charges (including 4 felony counts)](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=be06dd19f8&e=7017cc100e).
* As Chair of the Orange County Republican Party, Scott Baugh oversaw a scheme to commit rampant voter fraud by illegally registering voters, [a scheme that led to a dozen felony counts against GOP staffers](https://davemin.us7.list-manage.com/track/click?u=1b97cb6a343b55cba640c3404&id=6387defbf6&e=7017cc100e).

**###** _California’s 47th is an open Congressional District in Orange County that includes the Cities of Costa Mesa, Huntington Beach, Irvine, Newport Beach, and Seal Beach, and portions of Laguna Beach, Laguna Hills, and Laguna Woods. Incumbent Katie Porter is vacating the seat to run for U.S. Senate. In 2022, Porter defeated former Assemblymember Republican Scott Baugh by 3.44% in this “toss-up” district. State Senator Dave Min currently represents over 80% of Congressional District 47 in Sacramento. In 2020, Min received over 158,000 votes within CA-47, defeating incumbent John Moorlach by 5.15% in this area. 19% of the registered voters in CA-47 are of Asian and Pacific Islander descent, including one of the largest Korean-American populations in the country. _

body:

**The T47C and the RNC!****(Or... From Cows to Coconuts)****
**
Last month, I traveled back and forth to Florida twice, and drove across the state of Oregon six times! Stepping off the plane into West Palm Beach was quite a shift this time - from Baker County snow to 85 and sunny overnight. You'll see bright colors and plastic surgery everywhere you look, and if you strike up a conversation with a stranger, there's a good chance they're conservative. Florida is awesome.

The Trump 47 Committee Summer Retreat was coordinated along with the RNC, invitation-only to those who had proven their fundraising ability. Solomon qualified and represented Oregon. I've seen such a shift in the RNC over the past couple months, and it's a shift I like - a breath of fresh air watching a floundering organization shift into functional again. I would also love to see the Oregon Republican Party flourish. It's very helpful when state parties do well. But here, the party is busy dealing with a depleted bank account and an election scandal AND ongoing defamation lawsuit regarding our National Committeewoman/Ronna McDaniel Superfan Tracy Honl. Fun times.

Nationally and internationally, the political scene feels good for the Republican Party. Donors are coming back, polls for President Trump are through the roof, and I sat in on some sessions that broke down the internals of the Biden campaign vs. the Trump campaign, and more details as to how positions in the Trump Campaign dovetail with those in the RNC now. Again - a relief to see adults in control of the room.

Part of the weekend was at a hotel and the rest was at Mar-a-Lago, political figures present always. We had a mini Republicans Overseas (RO) Reunion with Worldwide Exec VP Jim Gosart and his wife, Chairman of the Board Bruce Ash, and Trump's former Ambassador to Thailand Michael Desombre who helped start the organization. We finally had a chance to catch up with Governor Kristi Noem, who spoke at our Worldwide Freedom Initiative last year to help push back against Davos/WEF. The WEF agenda affects the U.S. and Oregon, and goes hand-in-glove with the Democrat party apparatus.

People on social media questioned why Trump kept Speaker Mike Johnson in the spotlight with him over the weekend and why I even agreed to a photo with him, and it's just this simple: we can't turn the gavel over to Hakeem Jefferies and the Dems right now. I don't like how a few of those votes went, either. But I also know we can't give up committee control, toss away investigations, or hamstring Trump when he gets into office. My message is that sometimes you have to play the long game if you want to win in the end - especially if you're working with a one-vote majority.

clean_body: | | | | | The T47C and the RNC!(Or... From Cows to Coconuts) Last month, I traveled back and forth to Florida twice, and drove across the state of Oregon six times! Stepping off the plane into West Palm Beach was quite a shift this time - from Baker County snow to 85 and sunny overnight. You'll see bright colors and plastic surgery everywhere you look, and if you strike up a conversation with a stranger, there's a good chance they're conservative. Florida is awesome. The Trump 47 Committee Summer Retreat was coordinated along with the RNC, invitation-only to those who had proven their fundraising ability. Solomon qualified and represented Oregon. I've seen such a shift in the RNC over the past couple months, and it's a shift I like - a breath of fresh air watching a floundering organization shift into functional again. I would also love to see the Oregon Republican Party flourish. It's very helpful when state parties do well. But here, the party is busy dealing with a depleted bank account and an election scandal AND ongoing defamation lawsuit regarding our National Committeewoman/Ronna McDaniel Superfan Tracy Honl. Fun times. Nationally and internationally, the political scene feels good for the Republican Party. Donors are coming back, polls for President Trump are through the roof, and I sat in on some sessions that broke down the internals of the Biden campaign vs. the Trump campaign, and more details as to how positions in the Trump Campaign dovetail with those in the RNC now. Again - a relief to see adults in control of the room. Part of the weekend was at a hotel and the rest was at Mar-a-Lago, political figures present always. We had a mini Republicans Overseas (RO) Reunion with Worldwide Exec VP Jim Gosart and his wife, Chairman of the Board Bruce Ash, and Trump's former Ambassador to Thailand Michael Desombre who helped start the organization. We finally had a chance to catch up with Governor Kristi Noem, who spoke at our Worldwide Freedom Initiative last year to help push back against Davos/WEF. The WEF agenda affects the U.S. and Oregon, and goes hand-in-glove with the Democrat party apparatus. People on social media questioned why Trump kept Speaker Mike Johnson in the spotlight with him over the weekend and why I even agreed to a photo with him, and it's just this simple: we can't turn the gavel over to Hakeem Jefferies and the Dems right now. I don't like how a few of those votes went, either. But I also know we can't give up committee control, toss away investigations, or hamstring Trump when he gets into office. My message is that sometimes you have to play the long game if you want to win in the end - especially if you're working with a one-vote majority. The collapse in our fundraising this month has been dramatic. And with our final FEC fundraising deadline of the primary tomorrow, we need to have a BIG day. | [](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=bbb94c63dcdf44188219d4d4831f7cab&_e=VY7vNHr__cB_CygRBNVj4xpFY1RTry9KcnioQZi_Fw73X0J3-YAixogTWWax2BfqHUkMqHv-tsaMl8jMuTztVchxHiXqlGBkEsDYYQUFud_g1RJpuHfl6bwfU5cxAG6wf_8ZSmxAKE9YboilNr6Ncd2Ty1W3K6t92Y1eq1OaWwq_4jXyncD74ZXORmKq0iSD4is1z33NnLfcCPW4Z5xhvGAdwCO9vlibLgp_LsuvMnoyU7dHaJSckJ4Nc_kKQ82S0pdPFTZrM2f0PU_mvlRDR3RQVkbk0GIHDCbs4ZDw6z8If4hXgTVYwWP3bfhTIjQPWvVmAnnR0LxQ7ih6SwUlb5py8WhI98BvvBQ4BAgT6RL4Y4JlzW5sJqeIJREtaYapyF7hU6gwupZobv2SlHCHUQ%3D%3D)

_** **_ Fellow Conservative,

I’m unsure if you’re aware, but tomorrow marks the final FEC fundraising deadline ahead of Montana’s June 4th primary. And quite frankly, I hoped to be in a better spot.

Why?

Because getting dollars in the door this month has been tough. My finance team tells me it’s typical for fundraising to begin taking off as Election Day draws nearer, but that hasn’t happened for us. For a while, things seem to be sorting themselves out. We raised a decent amount of money in March and April, but once May rolled around, our numbers went downhill.

**But don’t take my word for it. I made the chart above to show how dramatically our fundraising has fallen off.**
[**CHIP IN $3 ->** ](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=bbb94c63dcdf44188219d4d4831f7cab&_e=VY7vNHr__cB_CygRBNVj4xpFY1RTry9KcnioQZi_Fw73X0J3-YAixogTWWax2BfqHUkMqHv-tsaMl8jMuTztVchxHiXqlGBkEsDYYQUFud_g1RJpuHfl6bwfU5cxAG6wf_8ZSmxAKE9YboilNr6Ncd2Ty1W3K6t92Y1eq1OaWwq_4jXyncD74ZXORmKq0iSD4is1z33NnLfcCPW4Z5xhvGAdwCO9vlibLgp_LsuvMnoyU7dHaJSckJ4Nc_kKQ82SnIM00Eag5TjK1IGYEMjrWgmsGUsFhcyA95NZIHNS2bMg5k9TTAsqDx-kl07Kqq3-wI8zeV6Qb3TyTY7fF1AuuSzUJZtQJ_wQjTd1Lipg8l1ooZZdgb3kLY6kzrF0ewJw0lW8qJ0ZlmQLx_GYKv1WNg%3D%3D)
Each value in the chart above represents how much my team raised in the first 15 days of each month so far in 2024.

Things were on the up and up through March , then we began to slide backward.

**I’m using bullet points because you must realize the precarious situation my team and I are in:**

* When we missed our April fundraising goal, I emailed our list of supporters, explaining how my campaign had been outraised by more than $5 million in Q1 and is regularly outraised by my opponent five to one. I’m not sure whether folks like you received my note, but to say say that request fell short is an understatement. **My plea for help raised just $931. ->[link to donate](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=bbb94c63dcdf44188219d4d4831f7cab&_e=VY7vNHr__cB_CygRBNVj4xpFY1RTry9KcnioQZi_Fw73X0J3-YAixogTWWax2BfqHUkMqHv-tsaMl8jMuTztVchxHiXqlGBkEsDYYQUFud_g1RJpuHfl6bwfU5cxAG6wf_8ZSmxAKE9YboilNr6Ncd2Ty1W3K6t92Y1eq1OaWwq_4jXyncD74ZXORmKq0iSD4is1z33NnLfcCPW4Z5xhvGAdwCO9vlibLgp_LsuvMnoyU7dHaJSckJ4Nc_kKQ82SLMo8hGY1o4-inb_ugUd5MaSrSuq9FC9YiW-Asq1yUL8LTTXzmloWcKmoXra32coigKqW9yJy4nYgyXzersX7Mzh1ozu0gC1PL2qllDDKMxbO2k2OF3afPQMajfldBZziHNuGTD4i0BWNp9QrVmJVyg%3D%3D) **

David McCormick sent out mailers to Pennsylvanians with _literal $1 dollar bills_ enclosed as part of his ongoing effort to win votes, flip this Senate seat red, and defeat Bob Casey.

body:
Last Monday we announced our second round of endorsements, bringing the number of young leaders we’re working to elect this November up 12!
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20240514-1&t=1&akid=690%2E587540%2EZzoeiv)
What a week, Peter!
**Last Monday, we announced our second round of endorsements, bringing the number of young leaders we’re working to elect this November up to _12!_**
From gun violence to climate change to the skyrocketing cost of living, our leaders haven’t been making enough progress on young voters’ priorities. So all over the country, we’re working to transform state legislatures (and Congress!) to include young people at a rate that’s closer to our portion of the population.
**[We'll get into more detail about each of the candidates we're endorsing below, but if you'd rather skip the long email and pitch in to help us get them elected in November, you can click here to donate $5 right now!](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240514?refcode=em20240514-1&amount=5&refcode2=690_587540_Zzoeiv&akid=690%2E587540%2EZzoeiv)**
Our endorsements span 10 different states in every part of the country.
In **Arizona** , first-generation American and Rhodes Scholar Oscar De Los Santos has already proven himself as a leader in the fight to repeal the state’s abortion ban. He needs and deserves our help to win re-election this year.
In **Tennessee** , abortion rights champion Allie Phillips and immigrant rights advocate and first-generation American Luis Mata are going to make fantastic additions to the state legislature.
In **Texas** , ER nurse Molly Cook will continue to be a powerful force advocating for abortion rights and public transit in the State Senate. She just won a special election to serve out the remainder of the current term, but she’ll need to be re-elected to a full term in November!
In **Florida** , climate advocate Nate Douglas will make sure young folks’ priorities are front and center, along with Bryce Berry and Ashwin Ramaswami in neighboring **Georgia.** And in **North Carolina** , non-profit leader and former National Guard Captain Dante Pittman will do the same.
In **Ohio** , we’ve endorsed Christine Cockley for the State House. She’s determined to make housing and childcare more affordable and keep our communities safe from gun violence — along with Anna Thomas, who we’ve endorsed in nearby **Pennsylvania.**
In **Montana** , Anja Wookey-Huffman is also laser focused on housing costs. As a born-and-raised Montanan who worked in Bozeman restaurants to fund her way through college and pay the bills, she personally understands the challenges young people are facing today.
And last but certainly not least, in **Delaware** , Sarah McBride has the chance to make history as the first openly trans member of the US Congress. She’s a badass state senator who’s been the driving force behind so many awesome bills, and we’re going to make sure she gets to take the fight to Washington next.
**If we elect even half of these candidates this November, we’ll have made monumental gains for young people's representation in government and a big boost to get young voters turning out by giving them people their age to vote for. But we’re not aiming to elect half of them — we’re aiming to help each and every one of them win on Election Day.**
**[So Peter, don't sit on the sidelines. If you're ready for a government that responds to the needs and priorities of young people, pitch in $5 today and help us elect all 12 of these fantastic candidates in November.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20240514?refcode=em20240514-1&amount=5&refcode2=690_587540_Zzoeiv&akid=690%2E587540%2EZzoeiv)**

She just won a special election to serve out the remainder of the current term, but she’ll need to be re-elected to a full term in November! In Florida , climate advocate Nate Douglas will make sure young folks’ priorities are front and center, along with Bryce Berry and Ashwin Ramaswami in neighboring Georgia. And in North Carolina , non-profit leader and former National Guard Captain Dante Pittman will do the same. In Ohio , we’ve endorsed Christine Cockley for the State House. She’s determined to make housing and childcare more affordable and keep our communities safe from gun violence — along with Anna Thomas, who we’ve endorsed in nearby Pennsylvania. In Montana , Anja Wookey-Huffman is also laser focused on housing costs. As a born-and-raised Montanan who worked in Bozeman restaurants to fund her way through college and pay the bills, she personally understands the challenges young people are facing today. And last but certainly not least, in Delaware , Sarah McBride has the chance to make history as the first openly trans member of the US Congress. She’s a badass state senator who’s been the driving force behind so many awesome bills, and we’re going to make sure she gets to take the fight to Washington next. If we elect even half of these candidates this November, we’ll have made monumental gains for young people's representation in government and a big boost to get young voters turning out by giving them people their age to vote for. But we’re not aiming to elect half of them — we’re aiming to help each and every one of them win on Election Day. — Leaders We Deserve HQ

EMILYs List has endorsed pro-choice champions in five swing states that need these leaders in office _more than ever_.
Since Donald Trump won **Michigan** , **Wisconsin** , and **Pennsylvania** in 2016 and lost all three in 2020, all eyes are on these three quintessential midwest swing states in 2024. Sen. **Tammy Baldwin (WI)** and Rep. **Elissa Slotkin (MI-SEN)** are running to protect two critical U.S. Senate seats. Reps. **Hillary Scholten (MI-03)** and **Susan Wild (PA-07)** are fighting to hold their seats in two of the toughest House races in the country, while **Ashley Ehasz (PA-01)** and **Janelle Stelson (PA-10)** are working hard to flip Republican-held seats in swing districts.

**Nevada** is similarly swingy. In 2022, Sen. **Catherine Cortez Masto (NV)** won reelection in Nevada _by less than one percent_ while Republicans flipped the governor's seat — also by a tiny margin. Sen. J**acky Rosen's (NV)** reelection race will come down to the wire — as will the races of Reps. **Dina Titus (NV-01)** and **Susie Lee (NV-03)** — but with our support, I'm confident they can _win_.

name: AOC
subject: Policy is personal.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Did you know that over half of all Members of Congress are millionaires? Meanwhile, the median household income is only $70,784. 👈🏽 **This is wild.**
Many of our lawmakers have no lived experience of working paycheck to paycheck or trying to pay rent working a low-wage job.
To me, policy is personal. When I worked as a bartender, I relied on tips to pay the bills. I know the urgent and daily stresses of working class people because I have lived them. And I intimately understand how important measures like raising the minimum wage, universal health care, universal child care, and free college can be for families living in financial uncertainty.
That’s why I’m in Congress: **to represent working families like mine.**
I am honored to be here, and I can’t do this work without you — the grassroots supporters who have had my back every step of the way. I can’t self-fund my campaign by writing a big check, and I don’t do any donor call-time or exclusive fundraising events.
[We rely completely on small-dollar donors, so if you are able, can you chip in $5 today to our campaign for progress?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20240514.EDoD30&refcode=em20240514-6405-P_FND_EGR_GOL&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=6405%2E2526796%2EH3FNv5)

Yours in service,
Alexandria

And with our final FEC fundraising deadline of the primary tomorrow, we need to have a BIG day. | [](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=eb2d552db72a4a36b183acc40a2ab752&_e=CE-q6nt3NYY9NQM813czWdLmMZhkiWD_CtkK0wnojuF0Be5aSwF_JbeJY15ZtcBQekhiSrrFz7DO7l48QymoDF2Ri5-04FeqGFJRp3BWdqi4Z5F6dcOUgINpTrA_af2_p-FucE2_sO4xccfJS4E-oGBdBay7qFlsDz1hic_zdhgvHAL3kbJM_6D-3k7A-tZge8tqjCBd_aCz64zc2ml9O1vPmRDZaovo-TwMK0F2T4Ut2QYm6FmR8BXNxQWIavX-jYjrx1eTS_2UrEmgkc6nYTXQg2oNLYQLN7T_1LIQjMRmgiftv0gVL-dixpzDwDlsSZcpendzHdqHji-yVoXVhWGNHJpFEG3qfNQOi2pgOlHwrR5kwU6gmWfEfIHLy7tB09_xYmgB0WGtS3Bdm06IzQ%3D%3D)

_** **_ Fellow Conservative,

I’m unsure if you’re aware, but tomorrow marks the final FEC fundraising deadline ahead of Montana’s June 4th primary. And quite frankly, I hoped to be in a better spot.

Why?

Because getting dollars in the door this month has been tough. My finance team tells me it’s typical for fundraising to begin taking off as Election Day draws nearer, but that hasn’t happened for us. For a while, things seem to be sorting themselves out. We raised a decent amount of money in March and April, but once May rolled around, our numbers went downhill.

**But don’t take my word for it. I made the chart above to show how dramatically our fundraising has fallen off.**
[**CHIP IN $3 ->** ](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=eb2d552db72a4a36b183acc40a2ab752&_e=CE-q6nt3NYY9NQM813czWdLmMZhkiWD_CtkK0wnojuF0Be5aSwF_JbeJY15ZtcBQekhiSrrFz7DO7l48QymoDF2Ri5-04FeqGFJRp3BWdqi4Z5F6dcOUgINpTrA_af2_p-FucE2_sO4xccfJS4E-oGBdBay7qFlsDz1hic_zdhgvHAL3kbJM_6D-3k7A-tZge8tqjCBd_aCz64zc2ml9O1vPmRDZaovo-TwMK0F2T4Ut2QYm6FmR8BXNxQWIavX-4UBeeFGs9U2g1lpaAIIgtfN0cIpwrshBIFcU_FtJnJzkx-Y6PMw9bn8J6pLlW31A7JD67iSfSjAk6Gj2Xszl9veC_tTPFMzEQu0OFGrn0IWhoW-Q7vRSZHmnwiNyOOCkJRWACNLOefh-yxJJYZCOpA%3D%3D)
Each value in the chart above represents how much my team raised in the first 15 days of each month so far in 2024.

Things were on the up and up through March , then we began to slide backward.

**I’m using bullet points because you must realize the precarious situation my team and I are in:**

* When we missed our April fundraising goal, I emailed our list of supporters, explaining how my campaign had been outraised by more than $5 million in Q1 and is regularly outraised by my opponent five to one. I’m not sure whether folks like you received my note, but to say say that request fell short is an understatement. **My plea for help raised just $931. ->[link to donate](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=eb2d552db72a4a36b183acc40a2ab752&_e=CE-q6nt3NYY9NQM813czWdLmMZhkiWD_CtkK0wnojuF0Be5aSwF_JbeJY15ZtcBQekhiSrrFz7DO7l48QymoDF2Ri5-04FeqGFJRp3BWdqi4Z5F6dcOUgINpTrA_af2_p-FucE2_sO4xccfJS4E-oGBdBay7qFlsDz1hic_zdhgvHAL3kbJM_6D-3k7A-tZge8tqjCBd_aCz64zc2ml9O1vPmRDZaovo-TwMK0F2T4Ut2QYm6FmR8BXNxQWIavX-XSYBio3b-ORzok5zoyH6N2-2OEcbXQeeMVKkL0fDf89TxWziAYXYeAVy07wF2GWSyAnhE86zjFZFJ17RSrf6_VrvnR6yspr0X7AMmXzyM3XSR4oCZBjBbzIYXdtwUS7fLTwBAKj_4sWmB2CI9s00vg%3D%3D) **

* We’re ahead in the polls, but it’s a statistical tie. The most recent national survey showed me leading my progressive opponent, Jon Tester, by 3%. **But in polling terms, this race is anyone’s to win or lose.**

* Republicans need to flip one seat to win the Senate majority. clean_body: The collapse in our fundraising this month has been dramatic. And with our final FEC fundraising deadline of the primary tomorrow, we need to have a BIG day. | Fellow Conservative, I’m unsure if you’re aware, but tomorrow marks the final FEC fundraising deadline ahead of Montana’s June 4th primary. And quite frankly, I hoped to be in a better spot. Why? Because getting dollars in the door this month has been tough. My finance team tells me it’s typical for fundraising to begin taking off as Election Day draws nearer, but that hasn’t happened for us. For a while, things seem to be sorting themselves out. We raised a decent amount of money in March and April, but once May rolled around, our numbers went downhill. But don’t take my word for it. I made the chart above to show how dramatically our fundraising has fallen off. Each value in the chart above represents how much my team raised in the first 15 days of each month so far in 2024. Things were on the up and up through March , then we began to slide backward. I’m using bullet points because you must realize the precarious situation my team and I are in: When we missed our April fundraising goal, I emailed our list of supporters, explaining how my campaign had been outraised by more than $5 million in Q1 and is regularly outraised by my opponent five to one. I’m not sure whether folks like you received my note, but to say say that request fell short is an understatement. My plea for help raised just $931. -> We’re ahead in the polls, but it’s a statistical tie. The most recent national survey showed me leading my progressive opponent, Jon Tester, by 3%. But in polling terms, this race is anyone’s to win or lose. Republicans need to flip one seat to win the Senate majority. That might sound easy, but entrenched incumbents, like Jon Tester, don’t have plans to lose, and they’re raising RECORD sums of money to buy themselves another term in office. -> Our trendlines shouldn’t be going down six months from the most consequential election of our lives. # Day 1 of Project 2025: Fire 50,000 Federal Employees
---
| [ ](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/maga-os?refcode=2025)
---
_**MAGA is attacking every level of government with Project 2025.**_ Nothing is safe if MAGA takes control after the 2024 election—**including the government employees who spend their lives serving this country.** If MAGA can gain control in 2024, Trump is going to attempt to reshape government at every level with his authoritarian ambitions in mind.🚨 UC Berkely found a frightening tally in their analysis of Project 2025, which they called 'Democratic Doomsday.' Here is their direct quote: **"If successful, Project 2025 would facilitate the firing of approximately 50,000 federal workers."** Federal employees are not just politicians and judges. They are also your neighbors working for the postal company, your family members working in the education system, and civilians who hold government jobs in various essential areas. From law enforcement officers and public health officials to scientists and engineers, federal workers play diverse roles critical to the functioning of our society. This proposal not only undermines essential public services but also exacerbates unemployment and economic instability. By prioritizing austerity measures over investments in infrastructure and social programs, Project 2025 threatens to deepen inequality and weaken the foundations of American democracy. Our federal workers play a crucial role in ensuring the smooth functioning of government services and programs that millions of Americans rely on every day. Slashing the federal workforce would not only disrupt these vital services but also harm the livelihoods of hardworking individuals and their families. We need to fight against Project 2025's plan to slash the federal workforce and advocating for policies that support our government workers and promote economic stability. Together, we can work towards building a stronger, more inclusive society that values the contributions of all its citizens. [**Join us in this critical battle to protect our nation from Trump’s authoritarian ambitions. Together, we can preserve the very essence of American democracy. Time is of the essence—your immediate action is crucial.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/maga-os?refcode=2025)

It’s official: April 2024 was the hottest April ever recorded on planet Earth. That’s horrifying enough. But March 2024 was also the hottest March ever recorded. Same deal for February 2024. And so on and so on and so on — 11 months in a row, all the way back to June 2023. Climate change isn’t a distant threat. It’s a clear and present danger. And I’m throwing everything I’ve got into the fight against it. We must build on what we achieved two years ago, when Democrats passed our nation’s biggest-ever investment in fighting the climate crisis, funded in part by my minimum tax on massive corporate profits. **So I just reintroduced the BUILD Green Act, which would devote $500 billion over ten years to electrify and modernize public vehicles and rail and build new electric transportation infrastructure across the country.** [**It’s exactly the type of bold action we need to take against the climate crisis. But it’ll be an uphill battle to get it into law. We’ve got to do this together. Will you add your name to say you support the BUILD Green Act and say you’ll fight by my side to pass it?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-buildAct/?source=EMZ20F_CLI_E_20240514_V1S1&t=8&akid=2171%2E4032634%2EZePeEV) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-buildAct/?source=EMZ20F_CLI_E_20240514_V1S1&t=9&akid=2171%2E4032634%2EZePeEV)

This legislation would accelerate us towards a clean energy future while creating 1 million new jobs, saving $100 billion annually in health damages, and preventing 4,200 deaths per year from air pollution.
Now, you might be thinking, This sounds great — but can it actually happen?
Here’s what I’ve got to say: part of it is already happening.
You see, after I introduced this bill back in 2021, an important piece of it ended up shaping the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.
It launched the EPA Clean School Bus Program with a historic investment in (you guessed it) clean school buses. I encouraged Massachusetts communities to apply for the funding. And earlier this year, I got to announce the money we’d won to help school districts replace polluting diesel school buses with electric or low-emission school buses.
We’ve already made real change with ideas in this bill — and we’re coming back for more.
**This legislation is one piece of how I’m staying in the fight against climate change. Big Oil and their GOP allies want us to bury our heads in the sand, but we see the threat we’re up against — and we’re taking action.**
